title.narrative: POO TO PRODUCT (P2P)

description.narrative:
Nawasscoal is a feacal sludge management company based in Nakuru, Kenya, producing renewable energy briquettes from waste. An in-depth analysis of the company's performance indicated the need for a thorough turnaround strategy, to get the company on track to break-even. This would enable the company to also secure additional funding and investments for the future.
The project to design and implement a turnaround strategy, includes a review the business model, craft a robust operational model, review institutional administrative structures, a critical review of the production process and an exploration of additional revenue streams as part of new business lines.

21-12-2023: Implementing the turnaround strategies advised by the consultant PES, the company underwent a significant transformation by shifting its business model from B2C to B2B. This change in approach has led to increased participation from businesses, with Nawasscoal now boasting a clientele of at least 150 high-tier customers who purchase in substantial quantities. These customers include factories, hotels, resellers, and institutions procuring directly from the company.
In addition to these business clients, there is a consistent flow of approximately 250 walk-in customers per month. These individuals are existing customers who visit the company's outlet shop at the parent company NAWASSCO and its site to make purchases.
While the upward price adjustment prompted some retail customers to revert to traditional charcoal due to economic challenges, the B2B model has proven to be a positive and successful strategy for Nawasscoal. | 14-12-2023: Nawasscoal experienced a growth in sales over the past 12 months, rising from 7 tons per month to 13 tons per month, resulting in an average of 10 tons per month. comment.narrative: 16-02-2023: The company did not make profit during the period. Nawasscoal has projected that, the break-even point and net profit will be achieved at sales of 23,000kg per month and above. However, this production capacity has not yet been demonstrated practically as it has not had sufficient time to be rolled out. Focus has been on implementing the experiments to reduce the production cost. As the new pricing is rolled out from August 1st and increased marketing efforts supported by WSUP are to start from September 1st, we expect to see the first substantial increase in revenue earliest end of September. The experiments have resulted in the potential to reduce the previous production cost from Kes. 34/Kg to Kes. 21/Kg.

21-12-2023: During the specified timeframe, the company incurred a net loss of 18%. This was derived from total sales amounting to KES 4,731,812, and total production costs standing at KES 5,776,875, resulting in a loss of KES 1,045,063 (Euro -8,196.5). Despite experiencing a significant 50% increase in sales compared to the preceding period, the company's initiatives to enhance factory operations, including improvements to the carbonizer and multiple trial tests for various products, contributed to an approximate 30% rise in production costs. As a result, the overall loss, when compared to the previous year on a comparative basis, was mitigated by 20%. Therefore, the net percentage loss amounted to 18%.
The determination of a net profit during this period proved challenging as a significant portion of the costs incurred consisted of consultancy fees and other project-related expenses, integrated within these overall costs. A more accurate assessment of the actual net profit is anticipated post-project completion. | 14-12-2023: In the audited financial year 2022/2023, up to June 2023, our company made significant strides in reducing gross loss, decreasing from KES 1,818,234 (13,400 Euros) in the previous year to KES 300,110 (2,200 Euros) this year—an impressive 84% improvement. This positive trajectory is aimed at establishing a favorable gross margin and, subsequently, achieving net profit. The challenges in gross profit were as a result of various experiments conducted to enhance plant performance and pilot different products, resulting in increased operational costs. Despite these challenges, the company demonstrated its capability to minimize losses and maximize profits through strategic initiatives such as revising selling prices and intensifying focus on institutional market segments, leading to higher sales revenues compared to previous years. comment.narrative: Baseline data collected at project level

20-12-2023: Considering an average of two bowel movements per day, an adult typically produces approximately 256 grams of feces daily, with 75% water content and 25% solid matter. Given this, a single person generates 1.92 kilograms of solid feces monthly. Nawasscoal utilizes an average of 7,000 kilograms of dry sludge each month in briquette production. To estimate the number of individuals benefiting from safe fecal sludge treatment, we can use the following calculations: Solid sludge produced by one person per day: 25% x 256g = 64g (0.064kg) Nawasscoal uses an average of 7,000kg per month of dry sludge, where 70% is utilized as fuel in the carbonizer furnace, and 30% is carbonized to be mixed with carbonized biomass like charcoal dust. Using the assumptions above to calculate the number of people benefiting from safe fecal sludge treatment per month: Solid sludge produced by one person per month: 0.064kg x 30 = 1.92kg Total treated by Nawasscoal: 7000kg Therefore, the total number of people benefiting from safe treatment per month is 7000kg / 1.92kg, which implies approximately 3,645 people.

Finally disaggregate users that are provided with a Safely managed / Basic service / Limited service from the initiative. The initiative must tick all criteria to be considered as that service level.
1) Safely managed service:
- the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs)
- the initiative's sanitation service is not shared with other households
- the initiative ensures that human excreta are safely disposed in situ or transported and treated off-site
2) Basic service:
- the initiative provides an improved sanitation facility (this includes: flush/pour flush to piped sewer system, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, composting toilets or pit latrines with slabs)
- the initiative's sanitation facility is not shared with other households
- initiative does not ensure that human excreta and urine is safely disposed / transported / treated
3) Limited service: Usually at baseline level, but cannot be included at target level. This includes, open pits, unimproved pit latrines, unlined pits, no slabs, prone to flooding etc
\* This is indicative of the reach and scale of the initiative in reaching new users with its products and services in terms of the service level that is being provided (as defined by JMP).

title.narrative: Other indicators (P) and narrative explanation
Please provide a short narrative explanation of the data here. (max 250 words)

actual.value:
Review of the production process and experiments were conducted successfully. The recommendations are being implemented in a phased approach with a view of achieving lower cost of production (from 34KES to 21KES per kg) and optimum output per day. Already implemented are: direct procurement of raw materials; utilisation of in-house maintenance capacity; procurement of additional agglomerators and hammer mill, carboniser improvements as well as additional drying racks with canvas cover.
· Sales increased from an average of 21.4 tons per quarter to 34.8 tons in the last quarter.
· Nawasscoal achieved an average of 83% on sales target compared to 46% in the last 3 quarters (Each quarter is 4 months).
· Increase in sales was due to;
i.Additional sales rep on contract for 6 months Increased sales activities i.e more online advertisements, visiting hotels and other institutions, partnering with cook stove manufactures i.e Botto solar, sales demonstrations events for our resellers
ii. Focus on institutional market segment – realized 30% increase in institutional market. Two new resellers on boarded and existing resellers supported to increase their sales
iii.Introduction of incentives i.e introduction of 30 days’ credit terms for bulk buyers, discount on prices for bulk buyers, delivery for large volume purchases

The data provided above emanated from the implementations of the project which involved the following;
Procurement Guidelines review: One of the major reviews is the inclusion of this clause that states ''_The_ _company shall source its raw materials directly from the communities around Nakuru as enshrined in the Public Procurement and Disposal Act Regulations 2020 Section 108 (M).” _This enables NAWASSCOAL to significantly reduce production costs. And increase community engagements hence increased beneficiaries.
Review of the production process. The recommendations are being implemented in a phased approach with a view of achieving lower cost of production (from 34KES to 21KES per kg) and optimum output per day. Already implemented are: direct procurement of raw materials; utilisation of in-house maintenance capacity; procurement of additional agglomerators and hammer mill, carboniser improvements as well as additional drying racks with canvas cover. Improvements done to the production line have resulted to confirming the potential of improved output of up to 20ton/Month. There are further improvements that have been recommended to achieve the set target of 25ton.
From January to June 2022 the company produced an average of 7 tonnes. In May and June 2022 the production was low due to the experiments and plant improvements taking place. Before improvements the company demonstrated in March 2022 ability to produce 12 tonnes.
In August (month of Election) NAWASSCOAL aims to produce 8 tonnes with projected increase to 10 tonnes in September. The company will thereafter continue to increase production as per sales up to 25 tonnes. es
